## E01: Workflow and sparse evidence

<!-- block: evidence-004 -->

[]{#evidence-004}


Source record: “Jobsearch Laya System 1,” 2026-09-29, with the architecture article's frozen-shadow analysis. Historical workflow result: 300/300 `survive`; option reversal and policy enrichment each changed 0/300 decisions. Separate sparse-shadow result: 18/149 label matches across twenty cards; 0/94 correct `not_stated` decisions. References are diagnostic, not human gold. Card-level dependence prevents interpreting 149 heads as independent observations. These results concern the tested routes, not every zero-shot model.

<!-- block: evidence-006 -->

[]{#evidence-006}

No invalid responses or reported input truncation; no configuration eligible; eighteen confirmation scenarios unused. Author labels are provisional synthetic references. ## E03: Native family comparison

<!-- block: evidence-010 -->

[]{#evidence-010}


Source record: “Council proxy references and System-1 evaluation,” final main report002, annotation appendix002 and supplementary report002, 2026-09-30. Fourteen lanes × 108 cards = 1,512 main records; 36 development and 72 confirmation cards per lane. Confirmation has twelve groups. Astra references: 36 valid development and 72 valid confirmation; Gemini: 35 valid development, one preserved invalid citation response, 72 valid confirmation. Confirmation status agreement is 58/72. These named report versions identify the reference snapshot; public summaries do not expose a complete reproducible judge/rubric manifest.

<!-- block: evidence-011 -->

[]{#evidence-011}


The separate twelve-card answer-annotation comparison includes the contradicted answer with Qwen relevance 0.99855. Perfect nDCG@3 on tiny three-passage retrieval slates is not answer correctness; token overlap already scored 0.9692. The 756 supplementary option-order calls are post-confirmation development diagnostics, not additional held-out confirmation. None of these references is human-adjudicated gold.

## E04: Prompt controls

<!-- block: evidence-013 -->

[]{#evidence-013}


Source record: “Laya prompt interventions,” 2026-09-30. Six fictional cases, four underlying claim families, eleven conditions, two checkpoints: 132 decisions. Each checkpoint matched 4/6 baseline references, with stable errors under tested meaning-preserving changes; evidence removal and decisive edits each matched 6/6 transformed references. Only four originally resolved cases count as resolved-to-unresolved transitions. A blinded assistant review agreed with authored references; this is model-reviewed synthetic evidence, not human gold or a reliability estimate.

## E05: Corpus-informed probes

<!-- block: evidence-015 -->

[]{#evidence-015}


Source record: “Laya training-corpus patterns and fresh prompt probes,” 2026-10-01. Public TRAIN corpus revision `d0e2f0c42fef86cc15d1688d25a19f5ba7c85b18`; cached base/typed model revision `55cf4c4ebb4ebe31b2550e8bdf3bd21b99753851`. Exact corpus-to-training-run correspondence is unverified. Thirteen fresh base cases generated 156 main predictions; five customer messages across three tiers and two models generated thirty more. Total: 186. Independent assistant references, no training-row evaluation, no untouched confirmation, near-replicates retained as a limitation. Base invoice matching improved 2/4 to 4/4 with rewording; typed matching fell 4/4 to 2/4 with generic keys; both duplicate classifiers remained constant at 2/4.

## E06: Expanded study status

<!-- block: evidence-017 -->

[]{#evidence-017}


Source records: “Expanded Laya prompt study” protocol and “Expanded Laya prompt results,” completed 2026-10-01. Fifty scenarios per task: 150 total, ninety development and sixty confirmation. Four fixed conditions on development produced 720 predictions. Frozen selection plus baseline produced 180 confirmation predictions:900 total. Cached base/typed revision remains `55cf4c4ebb4ebe31b2550e8bdf3bd21b99753851`; CPU, FP32, full-input cap 1,024 and head budget 192, with no reported truncation. No fine-tuning or new model weights. Independently reviewed synthetic references agreed with all authored labels; they are not human gold.

<!-- block: evidence-028 -->

[]{#evidence-028}


Selection required improved macro recall, at most one newly broken development case and no newly unsupported assertion on unresolved evidence; baseline wins ties. Base order operational wording improved15/30 to 21/30 but broke two cases, so remained unselected and unconfirmed. Selected confirmation results: base duplicate prose10/20 →10/20; base evidence prose13/20 →12/20; typed duplicate operational wording11/20 →12/20. Other model/task pairs retained baseline. The typed gain repaired one case without regressions, while exact-pair recall remained 2/10. Descriptive paired 95% intervals from 5,000 resamples of ten authored pattern clusters: respectively [0,0], [−0.15,0] and [0,0.15]. These characterize the fixture, not production reliability.

<!-- block: evidence-029 -->

[]{#evidence-029}


Ten shared patterns per task create dependence. Confirmation covers new cases within known patterns; some individual invoice discrepancy subtypes lack negative confirmation examples. Rejected variants are development diagnostics only. No repeated-run stability or target-domain calibration was established. Detailed contrasts include eight invoice repairs with two false alarms, five prose repairs offset by five regressions, and an evidence conflict changing between two wrong labels. These motivate scoped testing heuristics, not a universal intervention or deployment claim.

## E08: Memory feasibility

<!-- block: evidence-023 -->

[]{#evidence-023}


Source record: Laya architecture article, corrected steady-state VRAM probe. Eight-row micro-batch: 8.2186 GiB peak allocated, 8.9062 GiB reserved, 10.526 GiB free at process start. Synthetic 1,024-token rows, 256-token head, accumulation four, FP32 weights/gradients/Adam state, FP16 autocast and GradScaler, encoder/head checkpointing, second update completed. Auxiliary training operations and full end-to-end variation were absent. This supports limited memory feasibility, not task-training performance.

## E09: Bounded native robustness

Source record: “System-1 five-hour session,” 2026-10-02. Twenty-four newly authored development groups across people management, sponsorship and employment arrangement: six support, six denial, twelve unresolved, including three conflicts. Fourteen completed runs produced 573 native requests; all outputs valid, zero runtime failures. Smoke calls are included operational checks, not independent data. The 108 robustness requests per canonical lane reuse these groups. Provisional model-origin references were independently reviewed, not human-adjudicated gold.

<!-- block: evidence-031 -->

[]{#evidence-031}


Cached identities: Laya base English `55cf4c4ebb4ebe31b2550e8bdf3bd21b99753851`; DeBERTa NLI `6f5cf0a2b59cabb106aca4c287eed12e357e90eb`; Kev `9a45d25eb2ab761841196625383fa1dff0e56c1e`, frozen Qwen base `dc7cdfe2ee4154fa7e30f5b51ca41bfa40174e68`. Offline RTX 3060 FP32 inference; no text generation, training, downloads or paid calls. Laya's temperature-clamping warning was preserved; scores are uncalibrated. Kev reference kernels and native one-forward pointer execution limit performance interpretation.

| Canonical route | Facts correct /12 | Unsupported /12 unresolved | Assertions /3 conflicts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Laya | 11 | 9 | 3 |
| DeBERTa NLI | 12 | 7 | 3 |
| Kev | 12 | 6 | 1 |
| Frozen literal baseline | 9 | 0 | 0 |

<!-- block: evidence-032 -->

[]{#evidence-032}


Conflict assertions are a subset of unresolved assertions. The literal baseline matches 21/24 references with a narrow conservative quote/apostrophe guard. Standard NLI agreement excludes the three conflicts, giving a 21-case denominator; the overall 24-case safety stress includes them. This reporting distinction never overrides a prediction using the reference label. Kev bounded QA recovered 5/6 support and 6/6 denial, with 3/12 unresolved assertions and zero conflict assertions; no interface passed the frozen gate, and the conditional 324-request extension did not run.

Repeated labels disagreed on 0/24 for each canonical lane, retaining 10/7/6 endpoint errors for Laya/NLI/Kev. NLI counterfactual destinations were correct on 24/24, but both source and destination were correct on 17/24. Support removal errors were 4/6, 0/6, 1/6; subject-change errors 5/6, 6/6, 5/6 respectively. NLI distractor errors were 16/24; Kev's were 3/24. These dependent development diagnostics do not establish production reliability, minimal-negation causality, a capacity limit or a statistically superior model.

## E10: Frozen-head and prior holdout

Private canonical source records: frozen-head pilot, heuristic-prior development and one-shot independent holdout, all dated 2026-10-02. These records are not part of the public book projection. A frozen local MiniLM encoder fed sixteen registered small-head fits on synthetic grouped TRAIN/VAL (36/18 template families; 288/144 dependent rows). None met the joint exploratory screen of no more than 5% unsupported assertions on unknown references and at least 80% recall for both support and denial. T2/T4 shared recurrence and untied T4 were one-seed diagnostics, not an architectural verdict. The head-pilot TEST stayed unopened.

The V2 Python prior was frozen after one development correction. On familiar VAL phrasing it made 0/96 unsupported assertions and recovered 24/24 support plus 24/24 denial. A separate author produced 18 new synthetic holdout families (144 dependent rows); one label-free prediction and one provisional-reference scoring release followed. The resulting counts were:

| Holdout comparator | Unsupported /96 unresolved | Support /24 | Denial /24 | Coverage /144 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Abstain-all | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Fixed nonrecurrent T1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| Heuristic V2 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 4 |
| Consensus | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

All fail useful recall. Independent audit confirmed exact joins, split non-overlap and primary counts. A locked-scorer condition alias made its *aggregate* conflict denominator zero; the already saved condition slice has 24 conflicts and zero assertions for all comparators. No rerun or tuning followed. All references remain independently model-reviewed proposals, not human gold; three families per condition and repeated variants prohibit row-IID or real-world safety estimates. The held-out wording was longer and structurally different, but causal attribution of the collapse is unresolved. No component was promoted.

## E11: Frozen attention-routing diagnostic

<!-- block: evidence-035 -->

[]{#evidence-035}


Private canonical source record: “Zero-shot reranker attention and HRM-Text pilot,” 2026-10-02. The mask comparison used one extended authored passage from each of eighteen previously inspected claim families (three attributes × six evidence variations), with provisional independently model-reviewed references. Twelve references were unknown. Runs used frozen pretrained checkpoints, pinned isolated environments and paired same-input identity controls; no task fine-tuning or active-pipeline decision followed. The HRM-Text separate full grid had 144 dependent rows: 65/144 exact, including 20/24 support, 24/24 denial and 21/96 unknown, with zero invalid outputs.

<!-- block: evidence-036 -->

[]{#evidence-036}


| Native lane / selected exploratory mask | Correct /18 before→after | Key qualification |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| Laya base, narrow discontiguous hard mask | 9→14 | Six corrections, one regression; unknown unsupported assertions 8/12→4/12; descriptive paired sign p=0.125 before accounting for explored cells |
| Laya typed, same hard mask | 8→12 | Different corrections and a regression; no independent confirmation |
| Lev native pointer head, narrow 25%-overlap soft bias | 10→12 | Two unknown corrections; no new support or denial recognition; hard masks tied or worsened |
| HRM-Text bounded A/B/C, all tested masks | 9→at most 9 | No arm improved; its 144-row run is a separate, dependent diagnostic |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B bounded A/B/C, no mask | 12 | Answered unknown in every case, recovering zero support or denial |
| Nano-Jev grounded yes/no, no mask | 10* | Binary correctness only; denial and unknown cannot be distinguished |

<!-- block: evidence-037 -->

[]{#evidence-037}


*Nano's ten correct answers are on its native binary groundedness question, not the three-way relation. MiniLM and Qwen-Reranker relevance heads returned scores, not claim truth; their score changes do not establish ranking or factual-support gains. DeBERTa-v3 NLI rejected the generic 4D-mask route, so it has no valid mask result. Other catalogue identities remain model-specific feasibility work, not implicit negative results. At width 32/0%, the frozen reranker retained the entire supplied evidence string for 13/18 extended documents, tied by lexical ranking in every chunk cell; clause-level support was not checked. Laya and Lev identity masks reproduced raw logits exactly on all 36 and eighteen checkpoint-family checks respectively. Multiple mask cells were inspected, the passages place original evidence before appended context, and no fresh grouped confirmation was run. Accuracy changes cannot establish learned retrieval, generic compression, source-position or abstention-prior causality.
